claims.text: Clinic notes and structured electronic health record medication history often contain different medication information.
claims.poster_quote: Clinic notes and structured electronic health record medication history often contain different medication information.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Clinic notes and structured electronic health record (EHR) medication history often contain different medication information.
claims.reason: Abstract, first sentence confirms the claim directly.

claims.text: Outpatient notes may document medication starts, stops, holds, regimen changes, and formulation details that do not appear in the structured medication list at the same time.
claims.poster_quote: Outpatient notes may document medication starts, stops, holds, regimen changes, and formulation details that do not appear in the structured medication list at the same time.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Outpatient notes often record medication starts, stops, holds, regimen changes, and formulation details that may not appear in the structured medication list at the same time.
claims.reason: Introduction, first paragraph explicitly states this.

claims.text: Same-visit disagreement may reflect normalization errors, differences in terminology or timing, medication reconciliation practices, or actual documentation differences.
claims.poster_quote: Same-visit disagreement may therefore reflect normalization errors, differences in terminology or timing, medication reconciliation practices, or actual documentation differences.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Same-visit disagreement between these sources may result from note-side normalization errors, differences in terminology or timing, or actual differences in documentation.
claims.reason: Abstract, second sentence confirms the claim directly.

claims.text: Evaluating note-derived medications only against structured fields can confound note-understanding error with cross-source documentation mismatch.
claims.poster_quote: Evaluating note-derived medications only against structured fields can confound note-understanding error with cross-source documentation mismatch.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Evaluating clinic-note extraction only against structured medication fields can confound note-understanding error with cross-source documentation mismatch.
claims.reason: Introduction, second paragraph explicitly states this.

claims.text: Surface-exact matching achieved exact canonical agreement of 0.7226 on 5,403 held-out mention rows.
claims.poster_quote: On 5,403 held-out mention rows, surface-exact matching achieved exact canonical agreement of 0.7226, correctly normalizing 3,904 rows.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On 5,403 held-out mention rows, exact canonical agreement improved from 0.7226 with surface-exact matching to 0.8429 after lexical cleanup and curated alias mapping.
claims.reason: Abstract, performance results confirm the exact agreement value for surface-exact matching.

claims.text: Surface-exact matching correctly normalized 3,904 rows on 5,403 held-out mention rows.
claims.poster_quote: On 5,403 held-out mention rows, surface-exact matching achieved exact canonical agreement of 0.7226, correctly normalizing 3,904 rows.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Surface-exact matching achieved exact agreement of 0.7226, corresponding to 3,904 correctly normalized mention rows.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms both the agreement percentage and the normalized row count.

claims.text: Lexical cleanup increased agreement to 0.7749 and solved 283 additional rows.
claims.poster_quote: Lexical cleanup increased agreement to 0.7749 and solved 283 additional rows.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lexical cleanup increased agreement to 0.7749, solving 283 additional rows.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms the agreement increase and solved row count.

claims.text: Curated alias mapping increased agreement to 0.8429 and solved another 367 rows.
claims.poster_quote: Curated alias mapping increased agreement to 0.8429 and solved another 367 rows.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Curated alias mapping further increased agreement to 0.8429, solving another 367 rows.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms the agreement increase and solved row count.

claims.text: Safe decomposition produced no additional measurable gain, leaving 849 held-out rows unresolved.
claims.poster_quote: Safe decomposition produced no additional measurable gain, leaving 849 held-out rows unresolved.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The full deterministic pipeline remained at 0.8429, indicating that safe decomposition did not provide additional measurable gain on unseen patients.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms no measurable gain from safe decomposition.

claims.text: Lexical cleanup and aliases together solved 650 additional rows on unseen patients.
claims.poster_quote: Lexical cleanup and aliases together solved 650 additional rows on unseen patients.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The lexical-cleanup and alias stages together accounted for 650 newly solved held-out rows.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms the combined solved row count.

claims.text: End-to-end aligned extraction performance was precision 0.6129, recall 0.7140, and F1 0.6596.
claims.poster_quote: End-to-end aligned extraction performance was precision 0.6129, recall 0.7140, and F1 0.6596.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: End-to-end aligned extraction performance on held-out test rows was precision 0.6129, recall 0.7140, and F1 0.6596.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section explicitly states these metrics.

claims.text: Generic lexical retrieval reached only 0.7759–0.7768 agreement.
claims.poster_quote: Generic lexical retrieval reached only 0.7759–0.7768 agreement.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Generic nearest-canonical lexical comparators remained close to lexical-cleanup performance, with exact canonical agreement from 0.7759 to 0.7768.
claims.reason: Results, calibration comparators section confirms the agreement range.

claims.text: Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching reached 0.6519 when preserving matched terms.
claims.poster_quote: Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching reached 0.6519 when preserving matched terms.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A public OMOP/RxNorm synonym baseline that avoided project-specific alias refinement was lower still: 0.6519 when preserving the matched public term surface.
claims.reason: Results, calibration comparators section confirms the agreement value.

claims.text: Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching reached 0.5410 under ingredient-style collapse.
claims.poster_quote: Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching reached 0.5410 under ingredient-style collapse.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A public OMOP/RxNorm synonym baseline that avoided project-specific alias refinement was lower still: 0.5410 under stricter ingredient-style collapse.
claims.reason: Results, calibration comparators section confirms the agreement value.

claims.text: The predefined held-out treatment-context subset contained 1,073 notes and 2,805 reference note-label pairs linked to action-bearing cues.
claims.poster_quote: The predefined held-out treatment-context subset contained 1,073 notes and 2,805 reference note-label pairs linked to action-bearing cues.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The predefined treatment-context subset contained 1,073 held-out notes and 2,805 reference note-label pairs linked to action-bearing treatment-context rows.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms the subset size and pair count.

claims.text: The local extraction and deterministic canonicalization pipeline achieved precision 0.7355, recall 0.6435, and F1 0.6864.
claims.poster_quote: The local extraction and deterministic canonicalization pipeline achieved precision 0.7355, recall 0.6435, and F1 0.6864.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the full treatment-context subset, the local extraction plus deterministic canonicalization pipeline achieved precision 0.7355, recall 0.6435, and F1 0.6864.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms these metrics.

claims.text: MedXN produced output for 514 treatment-context notes.
claims.poster_quote: MedXN produced output for 514 treatment-context notes.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Untuned MedXN produced at least one prediction for 514 of these treatment-context notes.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms the MedXN output count.

claims.text: On the common subset of 514 treatment-context notes, the local pipeline achieved precision 0.7317, recall 0.6493, and F1 0.6881.
claims.poster_quote: On this common subset, the local pipeline achieved precision 0.7317, recall 0.6493, and F1 0.6881.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On this MedXN-output subset, the local pipeline achieved precision 0.7317, recall 0.6493, and F1 0.6881.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms these metrics.

claims.text: On the common subset of 514 treatment-context notes, untuned MedXN achieved precision 0.3884, recall 0.7704, and F1 0.5164.
claims.poster_quote: On this common subset, the local pipeline achieved precision 0.7317, recall 0.6493, and F1 0.6881, while untuned MedXN achieved precision 0.3884, recall 0.7704, and F1 0.5164.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On this MedXN-output subset, MedXN achieved precision 0.3884, recall 0.7704, and F1 0.5164.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms these metrics.

claims.text: MedXN recovered many reference pairs but generated substantially more false-positive note-label assignments.
claims.poster_quote: MedXN recovered many reference pairs but generated substantially more false-positive note-label assignments.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: MedXN recovered many reference pairs but produced substantially more false positive note-label assignments.
claims.reason: Results, external positioning section confirms this comparison.

claims.text: Only 4,563 of 27,752 note-derived rows, or 16.44%, had same-visit exact overlap with structured medication history.
claims.poster_quote: Only 4,563 of 27,752 note-derived rows, or 16.44%, had same-visit exact overlap with structured medication history.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Only 16.44% of note-derived rows had same-visit exact overlap with structured medication history.
claims.reason: Abstract and semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirm the percentage.

claims.text: 38.67% of note-derived rows had same-visit category-only overlap with structured medication history.
claims.poster_quote: Semantic and temporal relaxation recovered most apparent disagreements: 38.67% had same-visit category-only overlap.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Same-visit category-only overlap at 10,732/27,752 = 38.67%.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: 35.17% of note-derived rows matched within ±30 days after failing same-visit comparison.
claims.poster_quote: Semantic and temporal relaxation recovered most apparent disagreements: 35.17% matched within ±30 days after failing same-visit comparison.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ±30-day overlap after failing same-visit at 9,761/27,752 = 35.17%.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: 55.17% of note-derived rows had same-visit semantic overlap with structured medication history.
claims.poster_quote: Cumulatively, 55.17% had same-visit semantic overlap.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Cumulatively, 55.17% of note-derived mention rows had same-visit semantic overlap.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: 90.34% of note-derived rows had same-visit or ±30-day overlap with structured medication history.
claims.poster_quote: Cumulatively, 90.34% had same-visit or ±30-day overlap.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Cumulatively, 90.34% of note-derived mention rows had same-visit or ±30-day overlap.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: 96.03% of note-derived rows had some structured-history overlap.
claims.poster_quote: Cumulatively, 55.17% had same-visit semantic overlap, 90.34% had same-visit or ±30-day overlap, and 96.03% had some structured-history overlap.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Cumulatively, 96.03% of note-derived mention rows had some structured-history overlap.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: Only 1,102 rows, or 3.97%, remained in the strict no-structured-overlap bucket under broad project-level mapping.
claims.poster_quote: Only 1,102 rows, or 3.97%, remained in the strict no-structured-overlap bucket under broad project-level mapping.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Only 3.97% remained in the strict no-structured-overlap bucket under broad project-level mapping.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: Across 4,280 unresolved full-cohort rows after deterministic normalization, missing aliases accounted for 3,823 rows, or 89.32%.
claims.poster_quote: Across 4,280 unresolved full-cohort rows after deterministic normalization, missing aliases accounted for 3,823 rows, or 89.32%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Among 4,280 unresolved rows after the full deterministic pipeline, missing alias accounted for 3,823 (89.32%).
claims.reason: Results, residual deterministic-pipeline error interpretation section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: Lab, substance, or non-medication mentions accounted for 8.06% of unresolved full-cohort rows after deterministic normalization.
claims.poster_quote: Lab, substance, or non-medication mentions accounted for 8.06%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lab/substance or non-medication rows for 345 (8.06%).
claims.reason: Results, residual deterministic-pipeline error interpretation section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: Combination or formulation mismatch accounted for 2.52% of unresolved full-cohort rows after deterministic normalization.
claims.poster_quote: Combination or formulation mismatch for 2.52%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Combination or formulation mismatch for 108 (2.52%).
claims.reason: Results, residual deterministic-pipeline error interpretation section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: Ambiguous abbreviation accounted for 0.09% of unresolved full-cohort rows after deterministic normalization.
claims.poster_quote: Ambiguous abbreviation for 0.09%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Ambiguous abbreviation for 4 (0.09%).
claims.reason: Results, residual deterministic-pipeline error interpretation section confirms the percentage.

claims.text: The ten most frequent unresolved terms represented 87.64% of residual rows.
claims.poster_quote: The ten most frequent unresolved terms, led by acetaminophen, oxycodone, ondansetron, dexamethasone, and gabapentin, represented 87.64% of residual rows.
claims.label: supported

claims.text: Alias-aware deterministic normalization improved held-out exact canonical agreement from 0.7226 to 0.8429.
claims.poster_quote: Alias-aware deterministic normalization improved held-out exact canonical agreement from 0.7226 to 0.8429.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Alias-aware deterministic normalization improved held-out exact canonical agreement from 0.7226 to 0.8429.
claims.reason: Results, deterministic canonicalization pipeline section confirms the improvement.

claims.text: Random audit supported high canonical-label reliability among evaluable valid medication mentions.
claims.poster_quote: Random audit supported high canonical-label reliability among evaluable valid medication mentions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Random audit supported high canonical agreement among evaluable valid medication mentions.
claims.reason: Results, reference credibility and targeted audit section confirms the reliability estimate.

claims.text: Treatment-action attribution remained harder than canonical-label reliability.
claims.poster_quote: Random audit supported high canonical-label reliability among evaluable valid medication mentions, although treatment-action attribution remained harder.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Action correctness among evaluable valid rows was lower at 310/582 = 0.5326.
claims.reason: Results, reference credibility and targeted audit section confirms the harder attribution task.

claims.text: Broad-category visit-level concordance reached 0.4980 with mean Jaccard 0.3077.
claims.poster_quote: Broad-category visit-level concordance was materially higher than exact concordance: broad-category overlap reached 0.4980 with mean Jaccard 0.3077.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: At broad clinical-category level, concordance was materially higher: overlap rate 0.4980, mean Jaccard 0.3077.
claims.reason: Results, semantic note-to-structured-record concordance section confirms these metrics.

claims.text: Exact overlap reached 0.1918 with mean Jaccard 0.0435.
claims.poster_quote: Broad-category visit-level concordance was materially higher than exact concordance: broad-category overlap reached 0.4980 with mean Jaccard 0.3077, compared with exact overlap of 0.1918 and mean Jaccard 0.0435.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Exact level overlap rate 0.1918, mean Jaccard 0.0435.
claims.reason: Results, semantic note-to-structured-record concordance section confirms these metrics.

claims.text: Strict no-overlap combines note-side mapping failure, structured-side undercapture, extraction or reference noise, and a smaller set of plausible note-only medication evidence.
claims.poster_quote: Strict no-overlap should not be interpreted as proof of undocumented medication use. It combines note-side mapping failure, structured-side undercapture, extraction or reference noise, and a smaller set of plausible note-only medication evidence.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Strict no-overlap combines note-side mapping failure, structured-side undercapture, extraction or reference noise, and a smaller set of candidate note-only evidence.
claims.reason: Results, semantic-temporal mismatch characterization section confirms the decomposition.

claims.text: The cohort came from a private, single-center clinic-note environment.
claims.poster_quote: The cohort came from a private, single-center clinic-note environment.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The cohort comes from a private single-center clinic-note environment.
claims.reason: Discussion section confirms the cohort source.

claims.text: The canonical label space and broad medication categories were project-specific.
claims.poster_quote: The cohort came from a private, single-center clinic-note environment, and the canonical label space and broad medication categories were project-specific.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Both the canonical label space and broad medication categories are project-specific.
claims.reason: Discussion section confirms the project-specific nature.

claims.text: The reference set used LLM assistance, targeted review, and random review rather than exhaustive manual annotation.
claims.poster_quote: The reference set used LLM assistance, targeted review, and random review rather than exhaustive manual annotation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We constructed the reference resource with LLM assistance and targeted and random human review, but did not manually annotate every row.
claims.reason: Section III.B explicitly states that the reference set used LLM assistance, targeted review, and random review rather than exhaustive manual annotation.

claims.text: The reference set was packet-note-based rather than an independent span-annotated corpus over every manifest note.
claims.poster_quote: It was packet-note-based rather than an independent span-annotated corpus over every manifest note.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The reference layer is packet-note-based rather than an independent span-annotated corpus over every manifest note.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly states that the reference set was packet-note-based rather than an independent span-annotated corpus over every manifest note.

claims.text: The primary endpoint measures controlled note-side canonicalization within the constructed reference universe, not a fully independent corpus-level extraction benchmark.
claims.poster_quote: The primary endpoint therefore measures controlled note-side canonicalization within the constructed reference universe, not a fully independent corpus-level extraction benchmark.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The main normalization endpoint should be interpreted as controlled note-side canonicalization performance within the constructed reference universe rather than as a fully independent corpus-level extraction benchmark.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly states that the primary endpoint measures controlled note-side canonicalization within the constructed reference universe, not a fully independent corpus-level extraction benchmark.

claims.text: The base alias resource remains project-curated and institution-shaped.
claims.poster_quote: The base alias resource remains project-curated and institution-shaped.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The base deterministic alias resource remains project-curated and institution-shaped.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly states that the base alias resource remains project-curated and institution-shaped.

claims.text: Future work should test portability across institutions.
claims.poster_quote: Future work should test portability across institutions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Future work should evaluate portability across institutions.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly suggests that future work should test portability across institutions.

claims.text: Future work should improve public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels.
claims.poster_quote: Future work should test portability across institutions, improve public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Future work should evaluate portability across institutions, extend public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels, and test whether the same framework transfers to other treatment-context entities beyond medications.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly suggests that future work should improve public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels.

claims.text: Future work should extend the framework to other treatment-context entities.
claims.poster_quote: Future work should test portability across institutions, improve public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels, and extend the framework to other treatment-context entities.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Future work should evaluate portability across institutions, extend public ontology alignment for heterogeneous note labels, and test whether the same framework transfers to other treatment-context entities beyond medications.
claims.reason: Section IV explicitly suggests that future work should extend the framework to other treatment-context entities.
